facts.statement: The genus Trinacromerum was first described by Cragin in 1888.
Trinacromerum lived during the Late Cretaceous period.
Trinacromerum is an extinct sauropterygian reptile belonging to the polycotylid plesiosaurs.
facts.quote: Trinacromerum is an extinct genus of sauropterygian reptile, a member of the polycotylid plesiosaurs.

facts.statement: Fossils of Trinacromerum have been found in Late Cretaceous deposits in modern-day Kansas and Manitoba.
facts.quote: Specimens have been discovered in the Late Cretaceous fossil deposits of what is now modern Kansas and Manitoba.

facts.statement: Trinacromerum measured approximately 3 meters in length.
Evidence from its teeth indicates that Trinacromerum fed on small fish.
facts.quote: Its teeth show that it fed on small fish.

facts.statement: Trinacromerum's long flippers allowed it to swim at high speeds.
facts.quote: The long flippers of Trinacromerum enabled it to achieve high swimming speeds.

facts.statement: Richard Ellis described the physical appearance of Trinacromerum as resembling a "four-flippered penguin."
facts.quote: Its physical appearance was described by Richard Ellis as akin to a "four-flippered penguin."

facts.statement: The name Trinacromerum means "three tipped femur".
Trinacromerum is classified within the family Polycotylidae.
Trinacromerum belongs to the subfamily Polycotylinae.
The genus Trinacromerum includes species such as T. bentonianum, T. latimanus, T. kirki, and T. bonneri.
facts.quote: subdivision: Trinacromerum bentonianum Trinacromerum latimanus Trinacromerum kirki Trinacromerum bonneri

facts.statement: Trinacromerum lived in the Upper Cretaceous in what is now Kansas, United States.
facts.quote: que vivió en el Cretácico superior, en lo que hoy es Kansas, en Estados Unidos.

facts.statement: Trinacromerum had a body length of nearly 3 meters.
facts.quote: Medía cerca de 3 metros de longitud corporal.

facts.statement: Its teeth show that Trinacromerum fed on fish.
facts.quote: Sus dientes muestran que se alimentaba de peces.

facts.statement: The long flippers of Trinacromerum allowed it to reach high swimming speeds.
facts.quote: Las largas aletas de Trinacromerum le permitían alcanzar grandes velocidades de nado.

facts.statement: Trinacromerum lived from the Albian to the Maastrichtian stages, between 106.3 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Maastrichtian (106.3 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Trinacromerum is Trinacromerum bentonianum.
